note: The four `encoded_hex` values marked 'literal' are copied straight out of PeerCapabilitiesTests; the rest follow the same minimal little-endian rule.

encode.name: empty
encode.note: PeerCapabilitiesTests literal: PeerCapabilities([]).encoded() == Data([0x00]). Always at least one byte so an empty set is distinguishable from an absent TLV.

encode.name: bit_nine
encode.note: PeerCapabilitiesTests literal: little-endian, so bit 9 lands in the SECOND byte. Big-endian would give 0200.

encode.name: bridge_only
encode.note: Highest named bit still fits one byte.

encode.name: all_64_bits
encode.note: Eight bytes, the widest legal encoding.

decode.name: unknown_bits_survive
decode.note: PeerCapabilitiesTests literal: unknown bits are preserved verbatim, not masked to the known set.

decode.name: oversized_field_keeps_low_64
decode.note: PeerCapabilitiesTests literal: bytes past the eighth are ignored, so this decodes to .prekeys and not to something carrying 0xAA/0xBB.

decode.name: trailing_zeros_are_harmless
decode.note: Non-minimal encodings decode fine; only encode() is minimal.
